profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This Sabey Data Centers facility is part of SDC Ashburn in Virginia, one of the company seven current data center campuses alongside sites in Austin Texas, East Wenatchee and Seattle Washington, Manhattan New York, and Umatilla Oregon. Sabey own site states Sabey Data Centers was established in 2010 as a partnership between Sabey Corporation and investor National Real Estate Advisors. Sabey Corporation itself was founded in 1972 as a commercial real estate developer under founder Dave Sabey. The company data center business originated in Seattle during the dot com collapse when a vacated tenant building became SDC Seattle, building 5, prompting the pivot into data centers. Sabey Data Centers now operates six data center campuses nationally encompassing more than 3.5 million square feet developed over twenty years. No building specific address, opening date, or individual MW figures for the Ashburn campus specifically were located in available sourcing this session.

This specific row, the general Intergate Columbia campus row, already carried operator-sourced branding detail from a prior research pass, that this East Wenatchee, Washington facility is branded SDC Columbia and marketed on renewable hydroelectric power at 5 cents per kWh with room to grow, this session adds the operators own specific campus street address, 4405 Grant Rd, East Wenatchee, WA 98802, and the campus wide building count and capacity, three buildings on campus and a fourth under construction, totaling 70 MW.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Digital Realty is a publicly traded data center real estate investment trust. This session sourced two acquisitions that explain building names appearing across this operators rows in this registry. Per Data Center Dynamics trade press, Digital Realty completed a 7.8 billion dollar all-stock merger with DuPont Fabros Technology on September 15, 2017, adding 12 facilities concentrated in Ashburn, Virginia, which is why several Ashburn buildings in this registry still carry DuPont Fabros own ACC, meaning Ashburn Corporate Campus, naming convention. Separately, per Data Center Knowledge trade press, Digital Realty acquired the East Coast data center operations of AboveNet Inc. on October 2, 2006, for 40 million dollars, including a leased facility at 8100 Boone Boulevard, Vienna, Virginia, which is this registrys 8100 Boone Boulevard row. This specific row, recorded in this registry as a Digital Realty facility named Intergate Seattle East Building 4 in Tukwila, WA, is a significant correction rather than a simple address add. Intergate is Sabey Data Centers own registered campus brand, not Digital Realtys, and this operators own confirmed current Seattle area facility is separately branded SEA1, not Intergate. A datacenterHawk listing titled Sabey Data Centers Intergate.East Building 4, an exact match to this rows own Building 4 designation, gives 3433 South 120th Place, Tukwila, WA, and independently agreeing PeeringDB and DataCenterJournal listings confirm Sabey as the operator of this same Intergate.East campus. This session found no record of Digital Realty ever having acquired this specific Sabey campus, so this may represent either a past genuine change of operator this session could not further document, or an original labeling error in this registry, rather than a confirmed acquisition. reading:
Sabey Data Centers is a privately held, family-owned operator headquartered in the Seattle, Washington area. Its parent, Sabey Corporation, was established in 1972 by Dave Sabey, and Sabey Data Centers itself formed in 2010 as a partnership between Sabey Corporation and National Real Estate Advisors.

The company's own site describes a portfolio of six data center campuses, with more in development, spanning its original Pacific Northwest base in Seattle and the broader Puget Sound area, plus Columbia near East Wenatchee, Quincy, and Umatilla, Oregon, alongside campuses in Ashburn, Virginia, Austin, Texas, and Manhattan, New York. No precise total capacity figure in megawatts or square footage was located on the operator's site this session.

The registry here tracks 12 Sabey facilities across two states, Virginia and Washington, a narrower footprint than the seven-market list on the operator's own site, which additionally names Texas, New York, and Oregon locations. As one of the smaller family-owned operators in this registry, alongside CloudHQ's Fateh Family Office structure, Sabey's Quincy and East Wenatchee campuses sit in Washington's Columbia River hydropower corridor, a low-cost power region distinct from the AWS, Meta, and Google buildouts concentrated in Oregon's Columbia River sites tracked elsewhere in this registry.
